headline: Choose whether to extend or restart
statement: Return the largest sum of any nonempty contiguous subarray of nums.
intuition: At each number, choose between starting a new continuous section and extending the previous section. If the previous total is negative, it would make the new section worse. Keep the best total ending at the current number, and separately remember the best total seen anywhere.
approach: Initialize ending and best to the first value.
At each later value, compare starting fresh with extending ending.
Update the global best and return it.
correctness: Every subarray ending at i either starts at i or extends a subarray ending at i-1. Choosing the better option gives the best possible ending sum by induction. Taking the maximum over all ending positions therefore covers every nonempty subarray.
bruteForce: List every start/end pair and accumulate sums in O(n²) time.

complexity.explanation: Only two running sums are needed.

pitfalls: Initialize from the first element, not zero: all-negative arrays have a negative answer.
Return the global best rather than the final ending sum.
